Consonantal i

Theme

Time, the calendar & feasts

subsequent adjective

also following, the following day, the next day, ensuing, later (following)

classical

Liv. 2.18.1: īnsequēns annus (Lewis & Short)
Liv. 26.14.5: diēī īnsequentis pars

īnsequēns, īnsequentis

adjective, third declension (present participle of īnsequor)

following, next (in time)

Of the day, year or time that comes next; īnsequentī annō, in the following year.

Other words

  • posterus, postera, posterum — next, following

    also used · classical · Cic. Verr. 2.2.41: posterō diē māne (Lewis & Short); Hor. C. 1.11.8: quam minimum crēdula posterō

    Posterō diē is “the next day”; in posterum, for the future; posterī, posterity.

  • posterior, posterius — later, latter (of two)

    verb · also used · classical · Cic. Or. 21: nec acūmine posteriōrum, nec fulmine ūtēns superiōrum (Lewis & Short)

    Strictly where two are set side by side, the earlier (prior, superior) and the later.

Examples

  • multōs vērō in terrā Umbriā ūnum et eundem diem esse dīcere ā merīdiē ad īnsequentem merīdiem

    and that many in Umbria say one and the same day runs from noon to the following noonGell. 3.2.6

See also later, some time later, after.
